rules.statement: Keep `*.Abstractions` packages to contracts only; put any type with behavior (parsing, hashing, computing values) in a separate implementation or model library that the abstractions package references.
rules.why: The family rule is that no abstractions package contains logic; a model library holding the logic can be referenced by abstractions packages without breaking that rule.
rules.check: Look for method bodies with real logic, behavior-bearing classes or helper implementations added to a project named `*.Abstractions`.

rules.statement: Compute JWK thumbprints (RFC 7638) and thumbprint URIs (RFC 9278) from a parsed JSON Web Key model's required members, never from a hand-built or string-interpolated canonical JSON string.
rules.why: Hand-rolled canonical JSON strings are fragile and duplicate logic that the shared JWK model already implements once.
rules.check: Look for interpolated or concatenated JSON literals such as `{"e":...,"kty":"RSA","n":...}` that are hashed to make a `jkt` or thumbprint, or for code that pulls JWK members out of a raw JsonElement by hand to hash them.

rules.statement: Represent a JWK or JWKS with one shared JSON Web Key model from start to finish, not as raw `JsonObject`/`JsonElement` values that get converted to a DTO only when serialized.
rules.why: Several separate treatments of the same concept caused duplication, and a DTO that only appears at the serialization edges ends up bolted on instead of actually used.
rules.check: Look for new code that builds or passes JWK/JWKS data as `JsonObject`, `JsonElement` or ad-hoc result objects where the shared JWK/JWKS model type exists.

rules.statement: Back an immutable JSON-wrapping model with a detached `JsonElement` (from `JsonElement.Parse`/`JsonElement.ParseValue`) instead of a mutable `JsonObject` that needs defensive `DeepClone` calls.
rules.why: A detached JsonElement is immutable and owns no `JsonDocument`, so there is nothing to dispose or clone.
rules.check: Look for immutable model types that store a `JsonObject` field and call `DeepClone` defensively, or that keep a `JsonDocument` alive just to hold an element.

rules.statement: Use public constructors for model types that adopt an in-memory value (such as a `JsonElement`, a `JsonObject` or a collection), and a static `Parse(string)` method for deserializing text.
rules.why: The ADR makes this verb split the rule: a constructor adopts an in-memory value, and `Parse` deserializes text.
rules.check: Look for constructors that take raw JSON text, or for `Parse`/`From*` static factories that only wrap an in-memory node or collection.
